name: Epanetus
overview: Epanetus is a male believer recognized in the New Testament as the first convert to Christ from Asia. Beyond this unique distinction, Scripture does not provide additional personal details such as tribal affiliation or other notes. His mention highlights the early spread of the gospel beyond Jewish communities.
namesAndTitles: The name Epanetus appears only once in Scripture, in Romans 16:5, without any specific meaning or title attached. It is a proper name without a recorded divine origin or further explanation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Epanetus beyond what is indicated by his unique attribute as a convert. No additional relational details are provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Epanetus holds significance as a representative of the early Gentile believers, being noted as the first convert to Christ from Asia. His mention in Paul's letter to the Romans underscores the expansion of the Christian faith into new geographic regions. This highlights the global reach of the gospel message during the apostolic era.
